A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoARM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–E. The retained material can be matched despite bibliography relocation and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original benchmark accuracies, component ablations, token-consumption measurements, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains these original empirical results and adds benchmark results for MLVU and LVBench.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendices A and E retain the same hierarchical memory, five tools, controller loop, algorithm, and prompts. Model-name capitalization and explanatory edits do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Table 1 adds evaluation on MLVU and LVBench alongside Video-MME, LongVideoBench, and EgoSchema. This substantially expands dataset-level validation within long-video understanding, although the new datasets' task composition is not described.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds VideoLucy and Wang et al.'s VideoAgent to existing comparisons; the latter is distinct from the retained Fan et al. VideoAgent. The new benchmark panels also introduce GPT-4V, LLaVA-OV-72B, VideoChat-Flash-7B, and Qwen2-VL-72B, substantially expanding the comparator set.

E3.justification: The stated splits, accuracy metric, backbones, preprocessing, ten-step budget, and 200-question ablation subsets remain unchanged in Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix B. V2 supplies no separate split or procedure descriptions for the added benchmarks, so no additional protocol change is documented.

E4.justification: Tables 2–6 retain the model, tool, memory, step-budget, and sampling ablations. The efficiency analysis, subset-distribution analysis, failure case, and additional reasoning examples are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The retained Clip Analyzer confidence scores are individual model outputs, not new statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial comparative results, including VideoARM accuracies of 81.2% on MLVU and 79.7% on LVBench. It also adds VideoLucy's 72.5% overall Video-MME accuracy and Wang et al.'s VideoAgent at 60.2% on EgoSchema. Previously reported benchmark, ablation, and efficiency values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7, the token-cost derivation, Algorithm 1, and Appendix B's sampling formulation are retained. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or substantive derivations are added or revised.

C1.justification: Section 4.3 explicitly extends the benchmark-specific state-of-the-art claim to MLVU and LVBench. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims about adaptive reasoning, hierarchical memory, and reduced token consumption relative to DVD.

C2.justification: The interpretations of memory, tool use, sampling, and efficiency remain unchanged. Appendix C retains the same limitations concerning missed brief events, initial localization, and dependence on proprietary models.

D1.justification: V2 adds a front-page Code URL, providing new access information. Implementation settings, the detailed algorithm, and Appendix E's prompts and tool interfaces are retained; the PDFs alone do not establish the linked resource's availability.

R1.justification: V2 adds seven references and a focused comparison with VideoLucy, contrasting its text summaries and fixed backtracking with VideoARM's multimodal memory. The broader related-work organization and positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: V2 updates affiliations, adds acknowledgments, standardizes model naming, makes limited prose edits, and moves the bibliography before the supplementary material. The main narrative and appendix structure otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 1 becomes a composite display, with the retained comparison compressed beside two new benchmark panels. Figures 1–6 and the other tables retain their content and design, with limited spacing and page-flow changes.

improvement.justification: V2 provides broader empirical support through two additional benchmarks, adds a relevant VideoLucy comparison, and supplies code access information. These are useful but limited gains: the new benchmarks lack dataset and protocol descriptions, while the method, original experiments, and uncertainty reporting remain unchanged.
